questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren on and lights flashing. You are in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then pull to the right and stop. You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less for the curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less for the curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions coming up ahead. These signs often have speed plaques that show the safe speed for the area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and be more alert. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: On a slippery road, how should you change your following distance?

options.text: Keep it the same as normal.

questions.explanation: You need more time to stop your vehicle on a slippery road. Always keep a larger distance between you and the car ahead when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects judgment before other driving abilities. Alcohol travels from your stomach to your blood, then to other parts of your body. It damages the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is construction ahead. Drive carefully in this area.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed the same to get through the water.
Put the car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.explanation: To prevent skidding, avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect driving if taken in the recommended doses.
Medications are always safe to take if a doctor prescribes them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous and may affect your driving. Cold and allergy medications can make you drowsy and hurt your ability to drive safely. You are responsible for knowing how your medications affect your driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on one-way streets and roads where you are not allowed to enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp going the wrong direction.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, always yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of any medication that affects your driving is permitted:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, visibility is poor. A good way to show other drivers you are there is to turn:
questions.explanation: Use your headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Always use your low beam headlights when weather requires you to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to cross the centerline to pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see ahead far enough. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, where a solid yellow line is next to your lane, when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian, or in work zones where passing is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must obey the rule. This sign means you should not pass other vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not be, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions immediately ahead. This sign tells you to slow down and prepare for a sharp change in road direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid danger ahead.

questions.question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the intersection is clear and it is safe to pass through.

questions.question: Your car starts to skid with the rear end moving to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake. Steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This will straighten out your car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: When the road is wet or icy, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires grip less. You must slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mean no passing zone.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.
Go through the intersection slowly, but do not always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or intersection. Only move when it is safe.
